text_blocks.snippet: An anti-dumping investigation is a formal inquiry conducted to determine if imported goods are being sold at unfairly low prices (dumped) in a foreign market, potentially harming domestic industries. These investigations are triggered when a domestic industry believes they are facing unfair competition from dumped imports and can lead to the imposition of anti-dumping duties to offset the price difference and protect local businesses.

list.title: What is Dumping?
list.snippet: Dumping occurs when a foreign producer or exporter sells a product in a foreign market at a price below its "normal value." This normal value is typically the price in the producer's domestic market or a third-country market, or a constructed value based on production costs plus profit.
